reviews.review: It's a fine game if you accept it for what it is. It isn't the OG trilogy or even mass effect 4. It tries to be its own thing for better and worse. Fun Combat, great character side quests, meh main story lead to a package that is acceptable. It often goes on sale for $5 and below which at that price i find it a fine purchase. I miss good bioware.

My favorite Mass Effect. Same cool tactical sci-fi action as the previous titles, but more focus on open world exploration and discovery.

The Mass Effect trilogy is my favourite game series of all time. I grew up playing it, and I have more hours in it than I would like to admit. I bought this game on release on PlayStation 4 at the time, and I wanted to give it another chance with very realistic expectations after years of not revisiting it. I was inspired to do so after replaying the Mass Effect trilogy remaster, which I had a blast playing with my partner.

I modded Andromeda to make sure the experience would be as fun as possible and different than my previous 2/3 playthroughs. It was worse than I remembered and no amount of mods could save it. It really pains me to say, as I remember having fun when I was a teenager, however I now have a lot less free time and tolerance for games that I feel are wasting my time.

Obviously no shade if you enjoy it, but I sadly cannot recommend it. I really don't think anyone should play this, even if they are new to the franchise or Bioware games in general. The combat is the only decent aspect of the game, but it has not aged too well in my personal opinion. Everything feels clunky and rushed. The writing is a mess. I find the companions boring and dull. The exploration is more of a chore than anything else. I had more fun with Dragon Age: The Veilguard, and I would even go so far to say that game has more heart and better gameplay at least, despite it not being a masterpiece in any regard. 

I am not sure whether or not I should even hold out hope for Mass Effect 4, if it ever comes out. I am not convinced it should come out. Sometimes, loving a work of art means accepting its death, and even wishing for it. ♥♥♥♥ EA, ♥♥♥♥ capitalism, I miss Bioware.
